title: Hand Movements: A Window into Haptic Object Recognition
authors: Susan J. Lederman and Roberta L. Klatzky, 1987
research_question: To establish links between desired knowledge about objects and hand movements during haptic object exploration, and to determine the necessity, sufficiency, and optimality of these links for acquiring information about object properties.

participants.description: Experiment 1: 18 volunteers (11 females, 7 males), graduate students in psychology, ages 21-41 (mean 26 years), experimentally naive. Experiment 2: 48 student volunteers from an introductory psychology class, experimentally naive, no problems associated with sensory or motor hand function.
participants.recruitment: Volunteers (Experiment 1: graduate students, Experiment 2: introductory psychology students)

stimuli_or_exposures.description: 36 sets of three-dimensional objects. Each set comprised one standard object and three comparison objects. Objects varied across nine dimensions: texture, hardness, temperature, weight, volume, general shape, exact shape, part motion, and function. Irrelevant dimensions were decorrelated. Objects were held in place with two-sided tape or playdough in Experiment 2.

measures.instrument: Videotaped records classified into 8 EPs (Lateral Motion, Pressure, Static Contact, Unsupported Holding, Enclosure, Contour Following, Part Motion Test, Function Testing)
Percentage agreement on match-to-sample task (correctly identifying the best match for a specified dimension)
Pearson product-moment correlation, percentage overlap, item reliability score
Calculated as the difference between an EP's highest z-score performance and the mean of its performance under other instructions

mechanisms: Motor enhancement of sensory functions: The hand's motor competencies facilitate its perceptual and cognitive functions by allowing active exploration that generates varied sensory input.
Purposive hand movements: Specific exploratory procedures (EPs) are directly related to distinct dimensions of desired knowledge about objects, optimizing information acquisition.

Windows into haptic representation: Exploratory movements serve as 'windows' through which the underlying representation of objects in memory and the processes by which they are created and utilized can be investigated.
moderators: Desired object knowledge (instruction to match on a specific dimension)
implementation_implications: Guiding the development of robotic perception systems for manipulating and identifying objects by touch.
Informing the exploration and decision-making processes necessary for multisensor robots.

limitations: Scoring rules for exploratory procedures (EPs) were still under development, potentially leading to interscorer variability (though reliability checks were performed).
Some EPs (e.g., enclosure, contour following) were difficult to discriminate when brief or alternating rapidly.
Execution of one EP might inevitably involve another to some degree, potentially inflating the effectiveness of non-predicted EPs.

Constraining EP execution in Experiment 2 might have reduced the effectiveness of some EPs (e.g., enclosure was designed to eliminate unsupported holding, potentially underestimating its performance for global shape/volume).
Raw duration analysis in Experiment 1 did not account for inherent differences in EP execution times (addressed by z-scores).
